convertibility_reason: Uses iCustom to load 'DiNapoliStochastic' custom indicator (not a built-in MT5 indicator), and includes TradeAlgorithms.mqh external library for position sizing and trade execution logic

derived_values.name: TimeShiftSec - seconds per bar of indicator timeframe
min_rates_total - minimum bars required for indicator calculation

other_exits: Sell position closed when Stochastic Main > Signal (bullish crossover on bar[1])
Buy position closed when Stochastic Main < Signal (bearish crossover on bar[1])

position_sizing.conditional_logic: MarginMode enum controls sizing: LOT=fixed lots, BALANCE=fraction of balance, FREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin, LOSSFREEMARGIN=fraction of free margin minus loss, LOSSBALANCE=fraction of balance minus loss. MM=0.1 is either lot size or fraction depending on MMMode.

custom_logic_notes: Signal uses bar[1] vs bar[0] comparison: Ind[1]>Sign[1] confirms direction on the completed bar, then Ind[0]<=Sign[0] (or >=) on the current bar triggers entry - this is a crossover detection where the previous bar established direction and current bar confirms the cross. BuyPosOpen/SellPosOpen/SellPosClose/BuyPosClose are input toggles allowing independent enable/disable of each trade direction and close action. GlobalVariableDel_ called on deinit for cleanup. LoadHistory ensures bar data availability. Recount flag triggers recalculation on CopyBuffer failure.
python_conversion_notes: Custom DiNapoliStochastic indicator must be reimplemented or sourced separately - it is not a standard Stochastic. The TradeAlgorithms.mqh library provides BuyPositionOpen, SellPositionOpen, BuyPositionClose, SellPositionClose, and GlobalVariableDel_ functions - these must all be reimplemented in Python. The MarginMode conditional sizing logic (5 modes) needs careful porting. Entry logic is inverted crossover: confirm direction on bar[1] (Main>Signal or Main<Signal), then trigger on bar[0] cross back (Main<=Signal or Main>=Signal). SL/TP of 1000/2000 points may need digit-adjustment for 5-digit brokers - check if TradeAlgorithms.mqh handles this internally.
